notes: Revenue is the EUR 84.8m of income the club reported for 2024-25 (Palco23: EUR 84.8m against a EUR 77.36m budget; Crónica Vasca gives EUR 84,810,772); it is total income as the club states it, and the club received EUR 20.5m from player sales that season (El Correo), so it is not comparable with net turnover. 2024-25 net result after tax: EUR 212,159 profit (Naiz, Noticias de Álava); pre-tax not stated. Debt was put at about EUR 106m, up almost EUR 30m, at the December 2025 shareholders' meeting (Noticias de Álava) - a gross figure, so net_debt is left blank. 2025-26 budget: EUR 90,061,913. Stake figures for the Querejeta group differ within the same source (78% for his two companies, 83% for the group); no current shareholder register was found. Minority shareholders dispute the official 19,840 capacity (they estimate about 19,494) and the club reports 17,800 season-ticket members. Alavés voted with the majority on the 2021 LaLiga-CVC deal (the clubs against were Real Madrid, Barcelona, Athletic and Ibiza; Heraldo), but its allocation was not found. The club website (deportivoalaves.com) renders in the browser and its accounts PDFs could not be located. Not found: wages, operating result, pre-tax result, valuation, attendance, social follower counts, chief executive, tax ID.

Minority shareholders (including the Gurea DA - Accionistas Albiazules association)

ownership_summary: Controlled by Josean Querejeta, president of the basketball club Saski Baskonia, through his companies Lazkaokoa and Kiroletako Bazkideak, which together hold 78% of the share capital; his group entered in 2011 to rescue the club and took full control in 2016 (elDiario.es also gives the group's holding as 83%). The rest belongs to minority shareholders, some of them organised as Gurea DA - Accionistas Albiazules. The football and basketball clubs operate together as the Baskonia-Alavés group, which also controls 85% of Croatia's NK Istra 1961 through Circle of Life (since 2018). No fund or institutional shareholder was found.
